source.title: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban
source.summary: As of August, the number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran had reached another million.
source.evidence_text:
People were being expelled to Afghanistan from Pakistan and Iran, including some who had never visited Afghanistan.
One interviewee, Nazia, was born in Pakistan and crossed into Afghanistan with children.
Returning families encountered temporary accommodation provided by the UN and other aid groups near the border.
Families interviewed for the report described having little money and limited means of earning a living.
Aid agencies faced funding reductions while trying to support people arriving in Afghanistan.
A mother interviewed by the BBC expressed concern about girls’ futures because the Taliban restrict secondary and university education for women and girls.
The UN refugee agency said returns should be a matter of free choice and should protect people’s safety and dignity.
The report said both undocumented Afghans and people with registration documents were affected by Pakistan’s measures.
A Taliban minister acknowledged that the country needed assistance to cope with the arrivals.
Temporary border shelters were intended to house arriving families for only a few nights.
source.evidence_kind: Editor-written factual notes paraphrased from the linked BBC article; not quotations or independent reporting.

lesson.title: Starting again in Afghanistan
lesson.overview: Read a short report about people forced to return.
lesson.prediction: Read the title. What do you think the story is about?
discussion: What happened? Start with: The report says ___.
Imagine moving to a new place. Complete: I would need help with ___.
news_brief_sentences: People are being forced to leave Pakistan and Iran for Afghanistan.
Some people have never been to Afghanistan.
Nazia was born in Pakistan and crossed the border with her children.
Aid groups offer families a place to stay for a short time.
Some families have little money and no way to earn more.
They need help as they return and start a new life.

grammar.explanation: Have never been describes an experience that has not happened before now. Never means not at any time.
grammar.example_quote: Some people have never been to Afghanistan.

quiz.question: Which country are people being forced to return to?
options: Afghanistan
Pakistan
Iran
option_feedback: Afghanistan is the destination described.
Pakistan is one of the countries people are leaving.
Iran is one of the countries people are leaving.

quiz.question: What does the reading say about some people arriving in Afghanistan?
options: They have never been to Afghanistan.
They say they chose a holiday in Afghanistan.
They say they are opening a travel company.
option_feedback: The reading says some people have never been to Afghanistan.
The report describes forced return, not a chosen holiday.
The supplied report does not say this.

quiz.question: What does forced mean in this story?
options: Made to do something
Invited to choose freely
Given a travel suggestion
option_feedback: Forced expresses a lack of choice.
Free choice is different from being forced.
A suggestion does not mean someone must do something.

quiz.question: Choose the complete sentence.
options: I have never been there.
I have never be there.
I have never went there.
option_feedback: Use been after have in this pattern.
Be is the base form, not the required participle.
Went is past simple; this pattern needs been.

quiz.question: Who crossed the border with Nazia?
options: Her children
Her teachers
Her employers
option_feedback: Nazia crossed the border with her children.
The reading mentions her children, not teachers.
The reading says her children came with her, not employers.

quiz.question: What do aid groups offer families?
options: A place to stay for a short time
A paid job for every adult
A new home to keep forever
option_feedback: Aid groups offer a place to stay for a short time.
Some families have no way to earn money. A job for everyone is not promised.
The place to stay is for a short time, not forever.
